Hacker
HAK-er
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
From hack, to chop. In 1950s–60s MIT student slang a hack was a clever trick and a hacker an ingenious programmer; by the 1980s the press used the word for criminals who break into computer systems. In Gen Alpha game usage a hacker is a cheater — someone using "hacks" (aimbots, wall-hacks, speed or fly exploits, modded clients) — and "HACKER!" is shouted at anyone who wins too well, cheater or not.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To a Gen Alpha child a hacker is a cheater in a game — someone using secret tricks to see through walls, aim automatically, or fly. Kids also yell "hacker!" at anyone who beats them, fair or not. The Christian observation: the word holds two sins, and Scripture names both. The first is cheating. "Divers weights are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance is not good" (Pro 20:23). Paul uses an athlete’s rule: a man "is not crowned, except he strive lawfully" (2Ti 2:5). A game win stolen by hacks is no win at all, and a child who cheats in small things is practicing for large ones: "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much" (Luk 16:10). The second sin is the false accusation. Calling someone a hacker because he beat you is bearing false witness: "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour" (Exo 20:16). A father can tell a five-year-old: "Cheating is never okay, even in a game — God likes fair play. And we don’t say someone cheated just because they won. We say ‘good game.’" Teach both halves together: play fair, and accuse fairly.

Webster 1828 Definition

From MIT’s clever programmer to the press’s computer criminal to Gen Alpha’s word for a game cheater — and the false cry of "hacker" at an honest winner; Scripture forbids both the false balance and the false witness.

expand to see more

HACKER, n. (computing, 1960s; Gen Alpha game usage, 2010s–present) A cheater who uses exploits or cheat software in a game; loosely, any player suspected of cheating. "That guy’s a hacker — he’s flying."

Hacks — cheat tools: aimbot, wall-hack, speed hack, fly hack.

Older senses: an ingenious programmer (MIT, 1960s); a person who breaks into computer systems (1980s-).

Decode for parents: two lessons in one word — don’t cheat, and don’t falsely accuse.

Webster 1828, the root — HACK, v.t. To cut irregularly and into small pieces; to notch; to mangle by repeated strokes of a cutting instrument.

Key Scripture

Pro 20:23 — "Divers weights are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance is not good."

2Ti 2:5 — "And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully."

Luk 16:10 — "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much."

Exo 20:16 — "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour."

Modern Corruption

Hacker names the cheater who strives unlawfully, and in a sore loser’s mouth it becomes a false witness; Scripture condemns the false balance and the false report alike.

expand to see more

Children cheat in games for the same reason adults cheat at taxes: the reward without the work, and the belief that no one is hurt. Every hack takes something from the other players, and every hack trains the conscience to ignore small injustice. Luke 16:10 is the law of character formation.

The accusation side is just as formative. A child who calls "hacker" whenever he loses is learning to explain away defeat by slandering the winner. Teach him to say "good game," to check before he accuses, and to strive lawfully even when it costs him the round.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English haccian (to chop) → hack (clever trick, MIT 1950s–60s) → hacker (programmer; then intruder, 1980s) → Gen Alpha game cheater.

expand to see more

Old English haccian — to cut, chop

1950s–60s MIT slang: a hack, a clever trick; a hacker, an ingenious programmer

1980s press: hacker = computer intruder

2000s–2020s gaming: hacks and hackers = cheats and cheaters

Gen Alpha: "HACKER!" at any suspiciously good player

Usage

""He’s not hacking, bro, he’s just good.""

"He is not crowned, except he strive lawfully — no hacks (2Ti 2:5)."

"Thou shalt not bear false witness — don’t yell hacker at the winner (Exo 20:16)."
